content: Gaviscon is an over-the-counter medication specifically designed to manage symptoms of heartburn and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), commonly referred to as acid reflux. In the United Kingdom, it is manufactured and distributed by Reckitt Benckiser, while in the United States and Canada, it is produced by GlaxoSmithKline. The active antacid components in the UK formulation of Gaviscon include aluminum hydroxide and either magnesium carbonate or magnesium trisilicate. These ingredients work to neutralize stomach acid. Additionally, Gaviscon contains alginate, a combination of alginic acid and sodium bicarbonate. When ingested, the alginic acid reacts with the sodium bicarbonate to form a viscous, gel-like barrier that floats on top of the stomach contents. This barrier acts as a physical shield, preventing gastric acid from refluxing into the esophagus. The protective barrier created by Gaviscon not only reduces the frequency of reflux episodes but also provides relief from heartburn for up to four hours. In cases where reflux does occur, the barrier is the first substance to come into contact with the esophageal lining, offering a layer of protection against the acidic stomach contents. For optimal management of GERD symptoms, Gaviscon may be used in conjunction with lifestyle modifications. These include weight loss for individuals who are overweight, elevating the head of the bed during sleep, reducing alcohol intake, and quitting smoking. Unlike systemic medications, Gaviscon works locally within the gastrointestinal tract and does not enter the bloodstream, making it a non-systemic treatment option.
